items.title: Hyperdominant Left Circumflex Artery Challenging Conventional Paradigms and Current Guideline Recommendations: A Comprehensive Literature Review and Case Series.
items.abstract: Despite its rarity in the general population, left dominant coronary circulation with a hyperdominant left circumflex artery (LCx) has been associated with a more severe risk for ischemic and coronary artery disease. The concealment of an isolated posterior myocardial infarction (IPMI) on a standard 12-lead ECG among these patients with distinctive coronary anatomy can be concerning, especially when clinicians become trapped within conventional guideline-based diagnostic criteria, a circumstance that may ultimately be linked to a poorer prognosis. We present two cases that posed unique diagnostic challenges in this specific anatomical context. Case 1: A 63-year-old man presented to the emergency department (ED) with typical anginal chest pain and severe fatigue. Although the patient was initially diagnosed with non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), eventually a catastrophic occlusion of the left posterior descending artery (PDA) in the setting of a hyperdominant LCx was seen during coronary angiography (CAG). Case 2: A 69-year-old man arrived at the ED with typical angina, described as pressure-like. Although the serial 12-lead ECGs were completely normal, given the clinical context, the patient underwent an immediate invasive strategy in < 2 h. CAG revealed complete occlusion of the ostio-proximal segment of the left PDA. In both cases, hyperdominant LCx anatomy created a diagnostic blind spot within the conventional STEMI/NSTEMI paradigm, because the infarct territory was insufficiently captured by standard ECG criteria and failed to trigger guideline-based use of posterior leads or adjunctive imaging, thereby obscuring the diagnosis of IPMI. These cases warn clinicians about the diagnostic complexity of IPMI in a hyperdominant LCx setting. In such cases, ECG findings can be ambiguous or even completely absent, and the clinical presentation may not meet current unclear guideline-based indications for adjunctive diagnostic assessment, leading to delayed recognition of high-risk ischemia, particularly IPMI.

items.title: A Modular Polysaccharide Platform With Tannic Acid-Driven van der Waals Lock-In for Programmable Protein Delivery.
items.abstract: Protein delivery systems face persistent challenges, including low encapsulation efficiency, limited targeting ability, and lack of generalizability. Here, we propose a modular and programmable polysaccharide-based platform, enabling efficient encapsulation of a wide range of proteins, and tunable targeting across different cell types. The stepwise assembly applies tannic acid (TA) for protein surface stabilization. This rewires the encapsulation mechanism from unstable electrostatic binding to robust van der Waals-driven protein lock-in. The TA-protein complex can be encapsulated in an interchangeable polysaccharide nano-framework, exploiting the lectin-glycan recognition pattern to direct cell- and disease-specific targeting. The TA-Polysaccharide Encapsulation (TAPE) system robustly achieves > 85% encapsulation efficiency (EE) across a range of proteins, and tailoring the polysaccharide choice enables programmable targeting to distinct cell types. As a proof of concept, hirudin-loaded TAPE achieved targeted anticoagulant treatment in vivo. Overall, our work positions TAPE as a simple and generalizable platform that overcomes fundamental barriers in protein delivery, offering wide translational potential for protein-based therapies.

items.title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice.
items.abstract: Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice. Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80-86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73-84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6-25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5-5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36-54) mm Hg and 72 (60-87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5-9) mm Hg and 12 (9-15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27-43) mm Hg and 59 (44-70) mm Hg to 9 (7-11) mm Hg and 16 (14-23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively. TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

items.title: K-CVD as the Best-Calibrated ASCVD Risk Equation Among Three Country-Specific Equations in 9,532 Chinese Adults: A 9-Year Real-World Validation From CHARLS With Decision Curve Analysis.
items.abstract: Precise 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk prediction matters for Chinese primary prevention, while domestic risk equations have not been validated in 9-year real-world cohorts, and the Korean K-CVD model has never been validated locally. This study enrolled 9,532 ASCVD-free Chinese adults aged 45-79 years from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2020) with a 9-year follow-up (114 ASCVD events, incidence 1.20%). Three risk tools (pooled cohort equation (PCE)-US, China-PAR, and K-CVD-Korea) were compared regarding discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC)), calibration, and clinical utility via decision curve analysis (DCA); MICE was adopted to impute missing systolic blood pressure data. K-CVD presented optimal calibration (predicted/observed ratio = 0.97). PCE overestimated risk by 17%, and China-PAR underestimated risk by 10%. The three models had comparable AUCs (0.775-0.777, P > 0.05). Post logit recalibration yielded identical Brier score (0.0116) for all models. DCA showed negative net benefit at thresholds ≥ 5%; PCE and K-CVD gained slight superiority over China-PAR at 1-2% thresholds matching the low actual event rate. K-CVD has the best native calibration in this Chinese cohort. All three equations need formal recalibration for clinical use, and low cut-offs (1-2%) are more suitable for low-risk Chinese adults instead of Western standard thresholds.

items.title: Prognostic Value of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index and Controlling Nutritional Status Score in Patients Aged ≥ 75 Years With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
items.abstract: Malnutrition is common in elderly patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but its prognostic significance and the optimal screening tool remain unclear. This retrospective, single-center study aimed to compare the application of the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score in assessing nutritional status in very elderly patients with HFpEF, and to evaluate the association between nutritional status and clinical outcomes. A total of 196 patients aged ≥ 75 years (mean age 92.12 ± 4.28 years, 86.2% male) with HFpEF were enrolled. Nutritional status was categorized using CONUT and GNRI according to standard cut-offs. Patients with higher CONUT scores or lower GNRI scores (indicating worse nutritional status) had significantly longer hospital stays, lower levels of nutrition-related indices (albumin, total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), serum ferritin, transferrin saturation), lower lymphocyte counts, and higher NT-pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein (CRP), procalcitonin (PCT), interleukin-6 (IL-6)) (all P < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 11.5 months, 83 patients (42.3%) died. In unadjusted analyses, patients with worse nutritional status had significantly higher rates of all-cause death, all-cause readmission, and heart failure-related readmission (all P < 0.05). Multivariable Cox regression revealed that CONUT (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.366, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.181-1.579, P < 0.001) was an independent risk factor for all-cause mortality, while GNRI (HR = 0.962, 95% CI: 0.927-0.999, P = 0.043) was a protective factor. The CONUT and GNRI showed poor consistency (κ = 0.235, P < 0.01). Using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis based on vital status at the end of follow-up, the area under the curve (AUC) for predicting all-cause mortality was 0.86 (95% CI: 0.80-0.91) for CONUT, 0.79 (95% CI: 0.73-0.86) for GNRI, and 0.87 (95% CI: 0.82-0.92) for a combined model incorporating both scores via logistic regression. Net reclassification improvement (NRI) analysis showed that compared with the GNRI score, the NRI of the CONUT score was 0.580 (95% CI: 0.309-0.852), and the NRI of the combined score was 0.760 (95% CI: 0.499-1.022), both reaching statistical significance (P < 0.01). By contrast, the NRI was 0.083 (95% CI: -0.197 to 0.363, P = 0.560) for the combined score versus the CONUT score. Malnutrition is common in elderly patients with HFpEF. CONUT and GNRI scores are associated with adverse outcomes. Compared with GNRI alone, the combined assessment of the two scores improves predictive performance for adverse prognosis in elderly patients with HFpEF, while no incremental benefit is observed over CONUT alone.

items.title: p53 activation via pharmacologic MDM2 inhibition constrains exhaustion and enhances antitumor function of human CD8+ T cells.
items.abstract: Adoptive T-cell therapies using chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) or engineered T-cell receptors (TCRs) have transformed cancer treatment but remain limited by poor persistence and progressive T-cell exhaustion. Manufacturing strategies that promote memory T-cell formation may improve therapeutic durability. Here we investigated whether transient pharmacologic activation of the p53 pathway influences the differentiation and function of human CD8+ T cells. p53 expression was minimal in quiescent naïve CD8+ T cells but was rapidly induced following T-cell receptor activation. Pharmacologic inhibition of the p53 negative regulator MDM2 increased p53 protein levels and promoted expansion of central memory and stem-like memory T-cell subsets during clonal proliferation. Treated cells displayed enhanced mitochondrial fitness, increased polyfunctional cytokine production, and transcriptional programs consistent with memory differentiation and reduced exhaustion. Importantly, TCR-engineered CD8+ T cells generated in the presence of the MDM2 inhibitor Navtemadlin demonstrated superior tumor-cell killing in vitro compared with conventionally manufactured cells. These findings identify transient p53 activation as a pharmacologic strategy to enhance memory programming during T-cell manufacturing and suggest a clinically feasible approach to improve the efficacy of adoptive T-cell immunotherapies.

items.title: Regulatory network remodeling and potential non-canonical associations of the transcription factor SP1 during inflammation-to-cancer transformation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is closely linked to chronic inflammation, but the transcriptional mechanisms connecting epithelial inflammatory remodeling with malignant transformation remain incompletely understood. We integrated secondary analysis of published single-cell epithelial transition-state data, virtual SP1 perturbation, TCGA analyses, xCell immune infiltration analysis, TIDE-based exploratory immunotherapy prediction, Co-IP/MS, and a 4NQO-induced mouse model to investigate SP1-associated network remodeling during ESCC carcinogenesis. SP1 regulatory importance increased across pairwise epithelial state comparisons. In adjacent normal epithelial cells, virtual SP1 overexpression affected genes linked to inflammatory response, NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial stress remodeling, and proliferation. SP1 expression correlated with immune infiltration features and immune checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE analysis suggested an association with predicted immunotherapy-related features. SP1-binding partners were enriched in RNA metabolism, RNA splicing, and nuclear protein-complex annotations, suggesting potential non-canonical regulatory associations that require further experimental validation. SP1 may represent a progressively enhanced transcriptional hub during inflammation-associated ESCC carcinogenesis, with state-dependent network remodeling spanning epithelial inflammatory stress, malignant transformation, and tumor immune features.

items.title: The synergistic potential of combining PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapies in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is associated with a poor prognosis, and the efficacy of conventional therapies (chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery) remains limited. The advent of programmed death 1 (PD-1)/programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitors has substantially altered the treatment paradigm for ESCC. The combination of these immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with conventional treatments demonstrates significant synergistic potential. Standard oncological regimens often center on chemotherapy, radiotherapy, surgery, or various combinations thereof. This synergy stems from complementary mechanisms: conventional therapies can induce immunogenic cell death, release tumor antigens, and remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby laying the groundwork for immunotherapy. In turn, PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors work by releasing the "brakes" on T cells, activating and enhancing the host anti-tumor immune response. This facilitates the elimination of residual cancer cells and establishes long-term immune surveillance. In conclusion, the combination of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors with conventional therapy achieves a greater-than-additive ("1 + 1>2") effect and has evolved into a standard first-line treatment strategy for advanced/metastatic ESCC, substantially improving patient outcomes. Future research will focus on optimizing combination protocols, overcoming resistance, and precisely identifying patient populations most likely to benefit.

items.title: Case report: When encephalitis is not an infection: two cases of autoimmune GFAP astrocytopathy mimicking infectious encephalitis.
items.abstract: Autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) astrocytopathy is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disease of the central nervous system that frequently mimics infectious meningoencephalitis. Because its clinical presentation, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, and inflammatory markers often resemble central nervous system infection, diagnosis may be delayed, postponing appropriate immunotherapy. We describe two women with markedly different clinical presentations of GFAP astrocytopathy who were initially managed as suspected infectious meningoencephalitis. Both patients presented with inflammatory CSF findings, negative extensive microbiological investigations, and initial empirical antimicrobial treatment. In the first case, persistent aseptic meningitis with recurrent symptoms prompted autoimmune testing after repeated negative infectious work-up. In the second case, rapidly progressive encephalopathy requiring intensive care initially suggested severe infectious meningoencephalitis. In both patients, neuronal surface and paraneoplastic antibody testing was negative, whereas indirect immunofluorescence detected GFAP-IgG, supporting the diagnosis in the context of the clinical, CSF, neuroimaging, and microbiological findings. Both patients subsequently received corticosteroid treatment and experienced clinical improvement, although residual neurological symptoms persisted in the first patient. These cases highlight the broad clinical spectrum of GFAP astrocytopathy and its potential to closely mimic infectious central nervous system disease. Earlier recognition of GFAP astrocytopathy may facilitate timely consideration of immunotherapy and help reduce diagnostic delay and unnecessary antimicrobial exposure in patients with inflammatory meningoencephalitic presentations and negative infectious investigations.

items.title: Real-time exploration of the billion-scale human repertoire for precursor frequency analysis and rational antibody design.
items.abstract: The success of germline-targeting vaccines and rational antibody design depends on quantifying the population-level frequencies of specific antibody features, such as CDR lengths, sequence motifs, germline usage or preferred chain pairings, across the natural human repertoire. The maturation of high-throughput sequencing has generated large database repertoires containing billions of sequences, allowing researchers to assess naïve B-cell precursor frequencies and evaluate biologically plausible chain combinations. However, leveraging this scale of data remains a significant bottleneck, as current databases trap scientists between computationally demanding bulk downloads, restrictive, single-purpose web interfaces or outdated datasets. To address this gap, we introduce ABHunter, an automatically updated, open-access framework designed to explore and filter the healthy-human subset of the Observed Antibody Space (OAS) database, which currently stands at ~1.86-billion-sequence as of January 2026. Accessible via any web browser, the platform executes searches with median times ranging from 3.7 seconds for simple gene usage profiles to 20.8 seconds for complex paratope motifs, with full sequence retrieval completed in 118 seconds for 1 million hits. The interface allows users to quantify antibody feature frequencies to assess the natural abundance of targeted B-cells across various isotypes (e.g., utilizing IgM for precursor B-cell analysis), as well as map native repertoire contexts to scaffold isolated features. Additionally, it predicts biologically plausible inter-chain pairings for therapeutic design by using a statistical co-occurrence model that extrapolates pairing probabilities from the limited natively paired subset comprising 0.03% of the data across six donors. Furthermore, every search generates a comprehensive statistical landscape, detailing underlying complementarity-determining regions length distributions, amino acid compositions, and gene coupling patterns. For custom analysis and integration into bioinformatic pipelines, the optimized data structure reduces the storage footprint to 106 GB, allowing the entire tool to run locally on a standard laptop. ABHunter eliminates the compromise between accessibility and flexibility, transforming large-scale sequencing data into a universally accessible resource for next-generation therapeutic discovery. The platform is freely available at abhunter.org.

items.title: Established Versus Novel Strategies for Hepatitis B Functional Cure: A Cross-Regional Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Pegylated Interferon and Bepirovirsen Add-on Therapy.
items.abstract: Achieving functional cure (hepatitis B surface antigen [HBsAg] loss) and discontinuing lifelong nucleos(t)ide analog (NUCs) therapy are critical clinical goals in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) management. This study evaluated the long-term clinical outcomes and cost-effectiveness of different treatment strategies aimed at functional cure in hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative patients with CHB across Asia-Pacific income strata. A Markov state-transition model was developed to project 30-yr hepatitis B virus (HBV) disease outcomes in HBeAg-negative patients. Three finite strategies, PegIFN add-on to NUCs (PegIFN+NUC), switching from NUCs to PegIFN (Switch), and bepirovirsen add-on to NUCs (Bepi+NUC), were compared with lifelong NUC therapy. Analyses were stratified by country income level (high-income country [HIC], upper-middle-income country [UMIC], and lower-middle-income country [LMIC]). Costs were estimated from the health care payer perspective in 2023 USD. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), probabilistic sensitivity analyses, and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves were generated across a range of willingness-to-pay thresholds. Switch led to the largest reduction in hepatocellular carcinoma (31%) and HBV-related deaths (32%). In HIC, Switch was the dominant strategy (lower cost and higher quality-adjusted life years [QALYs] than standard care). In UMIC and LMIC settings, Switch remained highly cost-effective with ICERs of 1774 and 2200 per QALY gained, respectively. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated a >89% probability of finite PegIFN strategies being cost-effective at 1× GDP per capita thresholds across all income strata. In contrast, the bepirovirsen add-on strategy was dominated in all settings due to high acquisition costs and the impact of modeled seroreversion on long-term gains. Finite PegIFN-based combination therapies are cost-effective toward functional cure in AP region. While bepirovirsen represents a major milestone in HBV drug development, its current economic viability is limited by high costs and durability concerns. Policy efforts should prioritize optimizing established immunomodulatory combinations to accelerate global hepatitis B elimination.
items.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology

items.title: Association Between Hepatitis C Virus Infection and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains uncertain. This systematic review included observational studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for CAD outcomes among HCV-infected and HCV-uninfected adults. Adjusted hazard ratios, risk ratios, and odds ratios were combined on the logarithmic scale using a random-effects model and are presented as a summary relative association estimate with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by study design, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection status, and CAD outcome type; meta-regression evaluated follow-up duration, mean age, and the proportion of male participants. Twenty-one studies were included, representing diverse populations including veterans, people living with HIV, dialysis patients, and community-based cohorts. Fifteen studies contributed adjusted estimates to the quantitative synthesis. HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD (summary estimate 1.21; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40; P = 0.007), with substantial heterogeneity (I 2 = 72.1%). The association was statistically significant in cohort studies and in both HIV-specific and non-HIV-specific subgroups, although the HIV-specific subgroup was based on four studies. The myocardial infarction (MI)-specific subgroup was not statistically significant, whereas studies using broader CAD outcomes showed a significant association. Chronic HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD. However, substantial heterogeneity, differences in endpoint definitions and populations, residual confounding, and the combination of different effect measures limit causal interpretation and make the clinical importance uncertain. The nonsignificant MI-specific analysis further supports a cautious interpretation. These findings do not establish a cardiovascular benefit of antiviral therapy; prospective studies with standardized CAD endpoints and detailed data on renal disease, antiviral exposure, and lipid-lowering therapy are needed.

items.title: Hepatitis B Immunoprophylaxis rarely prevents molecularly evident subclinical HBV infection in children born to HBsAg-positive mothers.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains one of the most life-threatening human pathogens causing chronic hepatitis B and hepatocellular carcinoma in millions of people globally. Protective vaccines are available for decades, but their implementation is not yet universal. Mother-to-child transmission remains the prevailing route of HBV spread. Regardless of antiviral treatment of HBV-infected pregnant woman and neonatal immunoprophylaxis, HBV is transmitted at low levels to newborns as a subclinical (occult) infection at rates ranging from singular cases to the majority of the infant population examined in different centers worldwide. In the current study of 13 mother-child pairs, we applied a high-sensitivity molecular approach validated in previous studies, examination of different compartments of HBV occurrence, and testing of serial samples from infants followed for up to two years after birth to HBV-infected mothers treated or not with anti-HBV agent before parturition. All newborns received standard HBV immunoprophylaxis with HBV vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin supplemented with additional doses of both during follow-up. The data showed that the majority (84.6%) of the children investigated remained HBV reactive during the 24-month follow-up after birth at levels of ≤100 HBV genome copies per microgram of DNA, indicating that the prophylactic protocol was only at a low level (~15%) effective in preventing subclinical occult infection in newborns. Nonetheless, the same protocol inhibited development of overt HBV infection for at least two years after birth. In addition, the sequencing of the 360-bp HBV preS-S genomic fragment revealed homology between infants and umbilical cord blood mononuclear cells that diverged from the corresponding sequences in maternal plasma or peripheral blood cells in 4 of the 5 mother-child pairs examined. These data from the single-center study indicate that subclinical HBV infection in infants born to HBV-infected mothers is far more frequent than that reported and argue that virus transmission to newborns could be an inevitable consequence of maternal infection with HBV. This study also uncovered previously unknown HBV genomic discrepancy between infected mothers and their infants with occult infection suggesting the fetal and/or placental origin of the viral variant detected.

items.title: Associations Between Self-Reported Previous Hepatitis C Diagnosis, Hepatitis C Treatment, and Current Binge Drinking Among Persons Who Inject Drugs-National HIV Behavioural Surveillance, 2015-2024.
items.abstract: Persons who inject drugs (PWID) are disproportionately affected by hepatitis C virus (HCV). Excessive alcohol use among PWID can lead to more rapid progression of liver disease among persons with HCV. We assessed associations between ever reporting HCV infection, ever reporting HCV treatment, and current binge drinking among PWID who participated in National HIV Behavioural Surveillance (NHBS) during 2015-2024. NHBS conducted biobehavioural surveys among PWID using respondent-driven sampling in 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2024. We estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the association between self-report of ever having HCV infection, HCV treatment, and binge drinking in the past 30 days. The percentage of PWID reporting binge drinking was 25.8% in 2015, 24.0% in 2018, 13.3% in 2022, and 17.2% in 2024. In adjusted analysis, we found a significant negative relationship between self-reported ever having HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days in three of the four surveys: 2018 (aPR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.83-0.99), 2022 (aPR: 0.79, 95% CI:0.70-0.90), and 2024 (aPR:0.78, 95% CI: 0.65-0.93). We did not find significant associations between previously ever receiving treatment for HCV infection and binge drinking in the past 30 days across the four survey years. Among PWID, HCV infection was associated with reduced prevalence of binge drinking in 2018, 2022, and 2024. Our results support the importance of testing PWID for HCV infection and continued education on the harms associated with excessive alcohol use, including among persons who have received treatment for HCV infection.

items.title: Clinical Significance of Indeterminate Antibody to Hepatitis C in Cancer Patients.
items.abstract: Most patients with cancer are screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection using an antibody to HCV (anti-HCV) test. However, the importance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result is unknown. We investigated the clinical significance of an indeterminate anti-HCV result in cancer patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of cancer patients screened for HCV infection using ARCHITECT Anti-HCV at our institution between October 2016 and July 2024. Patients were categorized based on their anti-HCV results as patients with indeterminate anti-HCV and undetectable HCV-RNA in the absence of HCV treatment, and patients with reactive anti-HCV and chronic infection. We compared the two groups using univariable analyses and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Of the 112,180 patients screened with anti-HCV, 114 (0.1%) had indeterminate results; 101 of them with confirmed cancer were further analysed. Anti-HCV testing was repeated in 24 (24%) patients; most (84%) had non-reactive (46%) or indeterminate (38%) results. Among the 101 patients with indeterminate anti-HCV, 98 (97%) did not have proven HCV infection, but 3 (3%) had HCV infection. Multivariable analysis showed that male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.40-3.53, p < 0.001), age ≥ 60 years (aOR 1.61, 95% CI 1.01-2.56, p = 0.046), hepatitis B or HIV coinfection (aOR 3.13, 95% CI 1.21-8.11, p = 0.019) and cirrhosis (aOR 6.67, 95% CI 2.05-21.69, p = 0.002) were more likely to have chronic than an indeterminate anti-HCV result. Indeterminate anti-HCV results are uncommon in cancer patients and rarely indicate HCV infection.

items.title: Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the peroxisomal biogenesis factor proteins and interferes with lipid metabolism to affect the growth of liver cancer cells.
items.abstract: Primary liver cancer is the sixth most commonly diagnosed cancer and the third most common cause of cancer death worldwide. Chansu is made by processing and drying the white serous fluid of the posterior ear and skin glands of Bufo bufo gargarizans Cantor or Bufo melanostictus Schneider. Chansu is a well-known traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) that is mainly used for detoxification, detumescence, analgesia, the treatment of cancer, and heart failure. Cinobufagin, as a bufadienolide, has been reported as the main antitumor active component of Chansu. However, the molecular mechanisms related to the anticancer effects of cinobufagin still remain elusive. The purpose of this study is to explore whether cinobufagin inhibits the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells by inducing peroxisome dysfunction and interfering with lipid metabolism. The protein levels of catalase, ABCD3, PEX5, PEX6, and PEX10 in human hepatoma cells were analyzed by Western blotting. The effects of cinobufagin on the viability of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 cells were detected by cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay and clone formation assay. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) transfection was used to explore whether inhibition of PEX could enhance the inhibitory effect of cinobufagin on cell growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. The effects of cinobufagin on lipid metabolism were analyzed by untargeted metabolomics. The in vivo antitumor effects of cinobufagin were verified by animal studies. Cinobufagin causes peroxisome dysfunction in HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells. From a mechanistic point of view, we reveal that cinobufagin downregulates the expression of PEX5, PEX10, and PEX6. In addition, through RNA interference, cinobufagin partially blocks the growth of HepG2 and SK-HEP-1 tumor cells and restrains the expression of lipid metabolism-related proteins via downregulating the expression of PEX5 and PEX10. Subsequently, we perform a non-targeted metabolomics analysis of the cells and find that cinobufagin exerts its anti-hepatoma effects by interfering with lipid metabolic reprogramming. The results show that cinobufagin mainly interferes with glycerophospholipid and fatty acyl levels. In addition, in vivo experiments reveal that cinobufagin restrains tumor growth without obvious adverse effects. Serum metabolomics analyses reveal that cinobufagin causes significant changes in the levels of lipid and lipid-like differential metabolites. Cinobufagin is a promising natural drug for the treatment of liver cancer, and PEXs may be potential molecular targets of cinobufagin to exert anticancer effects. Cinobufagin induces peroxisome dysfunction through suppression of the proteins encoded by the PEX genes and interferes with lipid metabolism to restrain the growth of liver cancer cells.

items.title: Hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects of Arctium lappa root extract in valproic acid-induced toxicity: biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analysis.
items.abstract: Valproic acid (VPA) is a widely used antiepileptic drug; however, its clinical use is limited by hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis, primarily mediated through oxidative stress and inflammation. Arctium lappa root extract (ALRE) has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties that may confer protection against VPA-induced organ toxicity. Phytochemical profiling of ALRE was performed using GC-MS and HPLC. In vitro cytotoxic effects were assessed in Hep3B and PANC-1 cancer cell lines, while safety was assessed in THLE-2 normal hepatic epithelial cells and H6C7 normal pancreatic ductal epithelial cells using the MTT assay. The hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects were investigated in VPA-induced toxicity in male Wistar albino rats through biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological analyses. ALRE exhibited low cytotoxicity towards THLE-2 and H6C7 cells, with IC50 values of 1,084.92 and 1,174.62 μg/mL, respectively. VPA administration markedly increased serum levels of ALT (127.67 ± 4.34 U/L), AST (153.67 ± 4.91 U/L), ALP (178.67 ± 5.21 U/L), GGT (7.67 ± 0.09 U/L), amylase (47.33 ± 2.91 U/L), and lipase (49.00 ± 3.79 U/L) compared with the control group (p < 0.05). These enzyme levels were considerably lowered by ALRE administration, especially at 500 mg/kg. Furthermore, ALRE restored antioxidant defences (SOD, CAT, and GSH), malondialdehyde levels were decreased, and the histological architecture of the liver and pancreas was improved. ALRE effectively attenuated VPA-induced hepatic and pancreatic injury through antioxidant and cytoprotective mechanisms while exhibiting minimal toxicity towards normal hepatic and pancreatic cells. These findings support the potential therapeutic application of A. lappa as a natural protective against VPA-associated hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis. Further studies are warranted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and pharmacokinetic interactions underlying the protective effects of ALRE.

items.title: Prevalence of many comorbidities is similar irrespective of the time since HIV diagnosis in persons ageing with HIV who have survived to age 65 years.
items.abstract: To compare the prevalence of comorbidity in persons with HIV ≥65 years of age based on the time from HIV diagnosis. Cross-sectional observational cohort study. Data was collected from 540 participants in the CHANGE HIV (Correlates of Healthy Aging in Geriatric HIV) study, a longitudinal study of HIV in persons aged 65 years and older from seven primary and tertiary care centres in Canada between 2019 and 2026. We compared the baseline prevalence of comorbidities stratified by the cumulative time since known HIV diagnosis ( 30 years) and controlled for demographic, HIV and lifestyle factors. The cohort was 90% male, median age 69 years, 76% white, median CD4 561 cells/mm 3 and 92% with an undetectable viral load. They had a median of 3 (range 0-12) comorbid conditions. There was no difference in prevalence of coronary artery disease, dyslipidaemia, peripheral artery disease, stroke, chronic obstructive lung disease, asthma, arthritis, Parkinson's disease, HIV-associated neurocognitive dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, diabetes or liver disease based on time since HIV diagnosis. After accounting for confounders, longer time since HIV diagnosis was associated with higher prevalence of cancer, diabetes and peripheral neuropathy. Of the comorbidities only peripheral neuropathy, dyslipidaemia and Kaposi's sarcoma occurred at a younger age. Prevalence of many comorbidities was not increased in those with longer time since HIV diagnosis. Lifestyle factors (smoking, substance use and diet) are important contributors to non-infectious comorbidities in this population, and increased prevalence of cancer reinforces the importance of preventative screening.

items.title: Ascites Presenting as a Peritonitis-Like Manifestation and Liver Injury due to Trabectedin Monotherapy in a Patient With Myxoid Liposarcoma.
items.abstract: Trabectedin is a synthetic, marine-derived antitumor agent that exerts cytotoxic effects by binding to the minor groove of DNA. While trabectedin has demonstrated efficacy in advanced soft tissue sarcomas, hepatotoxicity and other adverse events remain concerns. However, cases involving drug-induced liver injury with ascites are rare. We report a case of an 82-year-old woman with recurrent metastatic myxoid liposarcoma who developed simultaneous liver dysfunction and ascites after 12 cycles of trabectedin monotherapy. Laboratory tests revealed Grade 3 hepatic dysfunction, and imaging showed accumulation of ascitic fluid. In the absence of infection or thrombosis, a diagnosis of trabectedin-induced liver injury with ascites was made. Supportive care, including hepatoprotective therapy, led to clinical improvement and resolution of the ascites. Hepatotoxicity is a recognized adverse effect of trabectedin, with proposed mechanisms including direct hepatocellular injury and cytokine-mediated damage. Peritonitis-like symptoms may arise from ascites secondary to hepatic dysfunction. In this case, hepatic dysfunction due to trabectedin may be the trigger for ascites presenting as a peritonitis-like manifestation. This case highlights the importance of vigilant monitoring during trabectedin therapy. Early recognition and management of liver injury and ascites presenting as a peritonitis-like manifestation are crucial. Further research is warranted to elucidate the mechanisms and risk factors associated with these toxicities.

items.title: Primary Liver Cancer and Other Malignancies in Alcohol Use Disorder and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease.
items.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption is a significant global health concern, causing over 200 adverse health outcomes, including liver disease, cardiovascular disease, neuropsychiatric disorders, and malignancies. Among these, alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) stands out as a leading contributor to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. Moreover, alcohol accounts for 27% of deaths from cirrhosis and chronic liver disease, with 30% of HCC-related mortality attributed to alcohol use. Despite its severity, abstinence from alcohol markedly improves survival, even in advanced stages of ALD, highlighting the centrality of cessation efforts in disease management. HCC represents a major global health challenge, especially in individuals with ALD. Unfortunately, HCC often presents at an advanced stage, limiting treatment efficacy and resulting in a dismal 5-year survival rate of 3.3%. Beyond HCC, alcohol use is linked to an elevated risk of other malignancies, such as cancers of the oral cavity, pharynx, larynx, oesophagus (squamous cell), liver (hepatocellular), colorectum, and female breast; compounding the disease burden. This review explores the intricate relationship between alcohol exposure, primary liver cancer, and other alcohol-related malignancies. It highlights the pathophysiological mechanisms, epidemiological trends, and the importance of alcohol abstinence in mitigating disease progression. Future research must focus on innovative approaches to improve prevention, surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment in this high-risk population. Drinking alcohol can cause liver cancer and several other cancers, including cancers of the mouth, throat, oesophagus, bowel and breast. People with alcohol‐related liver scarring (cirrhosis) are at the highest risk of liver cancer, which is often found late because many are not offered regular ultrasound check‐ups. Stopping drinking lowers cancer risk even when liver disease is advanced, and people with alcohol‐related liver disease should also have standard cancer screening and get help to stop smoking.
